title: AutoMetrics: Approximate Human Judgments with Automatically Generated Evaluators
claim: Small human feedback on outputs is distilled into a ranked set of interpretable, automatically generated metrics weighted by regression importance.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, dashed zoom lines linking data table to metric cards
description: The left panel is a table with a green header and three columns: Product, LLM Generated Description, and Human Feedback. Three example rows show product names with generated descriptions. Red X and green check icons mark the feedback, and a final row of ellipses implies more data. The caption below reads 'Human Feedback Data (Likert Scale, Thumbs up/down, Behavioral)'. Dashed black lines run from the table's corners to a stack of five blue-headed cards on the right. Each card names a metric: Prohibited Content Avoidance, Prompt Optimized LLM Judge, Tone and Voice (Rubric), Search Engine Optimization, and Examples-Based LLM Judge. Each has a small icon and a yellow percentage badge, from 26.3% down to 14.9%. A short description or prompt snippet sits under each name. The label 'Top 5 AutoMetrics' sits at the bottom right. The eye goes first to the bold green table header, then to the blue cards.
caption: AutoMetrics takes you from expensive measures to interpretable automatic metrics. Here AutoMetrics generates useful metrics for evaluating LLM written product descriptions from user reviews from EvalGen [ref]. Percentages indicate relative importance of each metric derived from regression coefficients.
abstract: Evaluating user-facing AI applications remains a central challenge, especially in open-ended domains such as travel planning, clinical note generation, or dialogue. The gold standard is user feedback (e.g., thumbs up/down) or behavioral signals (e.g., retention), but these are often scarce in prototypes and research projects, or too-slow to use for system optimization. We present AutoMetrics, a framework for synthesizing evaluation metrics under low-data constraints. AutoMetrics combines retrieval from MetricBank, a collection of 48 metrics we curate, with automatically generated LLM-as-a-Judge criteria informed by lightweight human feedback. These metrics are composed via regression to maximize correlation with human signal. AutoMetrics takes you from expensive measures to interpretable automatic metrics. Across 5 diverse tasks, AutoMetrics improves Kendall correlation with human ratings by up to 33.4% over LLM-as-a-Judge while requiring fewer than 100 feedback points. We show that AutoMetrics can be used as a proxy reward to equal effect as a verifiable reward. We release the full AutoMetrics toolkit and MetricBank to accelerate adaptive evaluation of LLM applications.
